data: This course looks at representations of history in fiction, film and auto/biography. Focussing on texts in English geographically ranging from England to South Africa, India and Australia, and temporally from the eighteenth century to the present day, we will examine the intersections of history and fiction in selected works from around the globe. What are the implications of reading a novel for its historical content or accuracy? How does the memoir or biography negotiate intergenerational histories and ideas of veracity? How do different writers reflect on questions of authorship and audience? How might archival research and films – documentaries, biopics, and adaptations – expand our readings of novels and histories? This is an interdisciplinary seminar which is designed to emphasise a high level of critical thinking and creativity. Students will be encouraged through their worksheets and their ongoing notebook assignment to be fully prepared and to contribute to each session productively, as well as to reflect on connections between each week’s topic. The final assessment is a visual archive essay which will require independent and original research, and which will be workshopped and presented to the seminar group at the end of term.
